events.body: Dropped the asmap update. I believe this is just an encoding issue where asmap-tool is not accounting for prefixes that are not supposed to be reachable. All asmaps more recent than the current embedding contain the problematic mapping.

Re fcfc1df041b8cecbc2bb4bf6836f5ba643f298a5 _contrib: Update fixed seeds_: All onion nodes were replaced. The new list is better (92% reachable vs 44%), but we should avoid complete swaps. Since `-onlynet=onion` implies `-fixedseeds=1`, this hardcoded list, from a single maintainer, is all it has to bootstrap with. This happens often (cc @achow101, @virtu) and can't be explained by random drift. The problem might be that we sort by `uptime` first, with thousands of 100.00% results, which are then sorted by `lastsuccess`. If the crawler moves in a predictable circle, then we'll get a different slice each update. In any case, it seems better to draw randomly from "good enough", and maybe not replace existing entries that are good enough. Otherwise the update looks good. I randomly sampled the removed nodes to see if they're indeed missing, and the added nodes to see if they're reachable: class | added | kept | removed -- | -- | -- | -- ipv4 (all entries) | 375/428 (87%) | 81/84 (96%) | 169/428 (39%) ipv6 (all entries) | 185/280 (66%) | 135/232 (58%) | 69/280 (24%) onion (sample of 128) | 119/128 (92%) | none kept | 57/128 (44%) i2p (sample of 96; kept sample 24) | 87/96 (90%) | 22/24 (91%) | 51/96 (53%) cjdns (all entries) | 4/5 (80%) | 3/4 (75%) | 0/7 (0%) - removed nodes were much less reachable than added ones, for each network - IPv6 nodes appear structurally less reachable than IPv4 nodes, even freshly added ones; not worrying, but maybe interesting for @0xB10C.
